frozen_rule.question: Is Earth flat?
frozen_rule.operative_condition: YES if conclusive proof Earth is flat becomes public by 2026-12-31 23:59 ET; otherwise NO.
frozen_rule.source_threshold_note: Frozen description does not define a special technical test for “conclusive proof.”

primary_public_evidence.published_or_updated_date: Not exposed in captured page metadata; current page capture only establishes public availability at observation time.
page_facts: NOAA describes Earth as an irregularly shaped ellipsoid, closer to an ellipsoid than a perfect sphere.
Page describes equatorial bulge from rotation, topographic relief, irregular sea level/gravity field and ongoing geophysical changes.
Page says the National Geodetic Survey measures Earth size, shape and gravity field; it describes satellite imagery using NASA Terra MODIS and NOAA GOES data.
primary_public_evidence.interpretation_limit: This is one current public NOAA fact page, not a full scientific-literature review and not a determination under the market’s undefined “conclusive proof” language.

scope_limit: No probability, market-price data, verdict, or exhaustive source search.
